name: Andean Ecuadorian Spanish

ancestors.notes: General Latin American Spanish (koine) — seseo/yeismo baseline shared by all LatAm varieties (Lipski 1994).
Quechua indigenous adstrate (regional contact influence; see stub qu.json).

notes: STRUCTURAL STUB. Andean (sierra / highland, Quito) Ecuadorian Spanish — Lipski's (1994) Andean zone; strong Quichua (Quechua) adstrate. Only the pan-Latin-American baseline (seseo: c/z->/s/; Lipski 1994) and the ⟨ll⟩–⟨y⟩ opposition below are modelled here; the dialect-specific phonology is deliberately not yet described (stub tier). Ancestry: es-ES-x-medieval -> es-ES -> es-419 -> es-EC -> es-EC-x-andino, with the indigenous adstrate(s) Quechua. Word-initial ⟨hie-, hia-, hio-⟩ keeps the GLIDE [j] rather than the es-ES parent's palatal obstruent, following the one rehilada variety for which this is documented: coloma2018 p.244 (cited by es-AR) prints hielo [ˈjelo] beside llama [ˈʃama], so the ⟨hi⟩ words do not join the merger there. EXTENDED BY ANALOGY to this lect because it is rehilada on the same axis; it is not separately attested here and NEEDS A NATIVE CHECK. ⟨LL⟩ AND ⟨Y⟩ STAY APART: ⟨ll⟩ is the groove fricative [ʒ] and ⟨y⟩ keeps the inherited [ʝ], so halla [ˈaʒa] and haya [ˈaʝa] are a minimal pair. Lipski (2011, p. 5): «In Quito and other northern highland areas of Ecuador, the lateral pronunciation of /ʎ/ gives way to a groove fricative pronunciation [ʒ], but the opposition /ʎ/-/ʝ/ is still maintained (e.g., halla [ˈa.ʒa] ‘he/she finds’ – haya [ˈa.ʝa] ‘that he/she may have’) (Haboud and de la Vega 2008).»

sources.author: Lipski, John M.

sources.notes: READ (geo.pdf). Reproduces the Lipski (1994) geographical dialect-zone classification of Latin American Spanish (list (2)): Mexican/SW-US; Caribbean; Guatemala-Yucatan-Costa Rica; El Salvador-Honduras-Nicaragua; interior Colombia + highland Venezuela; Pacific coast Colombia/Ecuador/Peru; Andean (Ecuador/Peru/Bolivia/NW-Argentina/NE-Chile); Chile; Paraguay/NE-Argentina/E-Bolivia; Argentina/Uruguay. Used here to enumerate the regional zones, and p. 5 for the ⟨ll⟩ [ʒ] against ⟨y⟩ [ʝ] opposition of Quito.
